- `action(actions, intent=...)` defaults to `intent='explore'`: an explore action that turns out `no_impact` STOPS the rest of that batch (`stop_reason='no_impact_action'`) and returns so you re-ground, instead of wasting the queued actions on a plan the environment just disproved. It only asks you to rewrite when it mispredicts (`hud_model: stale`, e.g. a refill or a new level). No HUD in this game? The harness re-verifies it against every action and, while its bar prediction holds, uses it (`no_impact_source: model`) instead of the statistical band -- you write it ONCE and it then runs free every turn with no further tokens. It only asks you to rewrite when it mispredicts (`hud_model: stale`, e.g. a refill or a new level). No HUD in this game? Don't write one -- the statistical fallback handles it (`no_impact_source: band` or `exact`).

After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.

Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.

- `current_frame` is always the settled board after your last action -- on its own it is enough for a purely static reading, and you never have to look further.

After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.

Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.

Motion may be meaningful (an object sliding, a chain reaction, a knock-on effect) OR incidental (a decorative transition, a flashing timer/HUD, a cosmetic redraw). Treat multi-frame motion as a HYPOTHESIS to test against the puzzle, not a fact. Reading `last_animation` costs tokens only when you inspect it, so pull it only when you expect it to help.
